transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2027-05-14 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Shah (Redwood AE), Dana Park (Redwood SE), Rhett Morales (CTO, Orbit), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Jules Carter (Infra Lead)

Summary:
Orbit Analytics is evaluating Redwood for a retrieval + rerank pipeline. They currently run Milvus for nearest-neighbor and are considering moving embedding generation + rerank to a managed offering to reduce infra ops. Main concerns: throughput (peak 2k QPS, sustained 400 QPS), embedding dimensionality tradeoffs (1536 vs 768), hybrid search + rerank latency, and deployment mode options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC). They also asked about SOC 2, network isolation, and cost tradeoffs.

Topics covered:
- Current stack & pain points
- QPS/throughput and tail latency targets
- Embedding dimensions and rerank model costs
- Hybrid search (ANN fanout + rerank strategy)
- Integration with vector DB (Milvus) and caching patterns
- Deployment options: hosted, dedicated, private VPC/on-prem
- Security/compliance: SOC 2, SSO, audit logs

Action items recap (from call):
- Samir to send pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated) and basic TCO calc.
- Dana to draft perf test plan and coordinate baseline runs.
- Jules to share sample dataset + expected query distribution.

Transcript:
00:00 Samir Shah: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see Rhett, Priya, Jules — welcome. we got about 45 minutes, we want to understand your retrieval pipeline and what success looks like.
00:14 Rhett Morales: yeah thanks, um so quick background — we're Orbit Analytics, we're building a semantic search layer on top of our product telemetry, so queries are high cardinality, we need sub-second responses ideally. right now we've got Milvus in k8s, Priya handles the models.
00:28 Priya Singh: hey, hi. yes we do embeddings with an open model, 1536 dims, but we've been experimenting with smaller dims to cut cost. our top requirement is relevance, second is latency.
00:41 Jules Carter: infra note: we see big spikes during customer demos—roughly 2k QPS bursts for a few minutes, sustained maybe 300–500 QPS. we're trying to avoid massive over-provisioning.
00:55 Dana Park: got it. to confirm, are you doing candidate generation in Milvus then reranking in your application? or is rerank co-located?
01:06 Priya Singh: candidate gen is Milvus, we pull top 200 and then run a cross-encoder rerank on CPU nodes today — which is slow. that's why we're thinking about moving rerank to GPU or using a managed rerank to reduce ops.
01:22 Samir Shah: on the Redwood side, you can choose hosted API for embedding + rerank or Dedicated pools for predictable throughput. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity that handles continuous high QPS without noisy neighbors. Private/VPC is an option if you need network isolation.
01:37 Rhett Morales: what kind of tail latency can you hit for a combined flow — say 200 candidate fanout then rerank? our SLO is 700ms p95, ideally 300–400ms.
01:50 Dana Park: rough numbers — if you do 200 candidates and run a small cross-encoder on a GPU-optimized runtime, we can hit mid-200s ms p95 for rerank alone with batching tuned. end-to-end also depends on vector DB fetch time. with our KV/prefix caching and local ANN routing it can be close, but Milvus fetches over network add variance.
02:10 Jules Carter: this is the part we worry about — network fetch + qps spikes. could Redwood host the vector DB or would we keep Milvus?
02:22 Samir Shah: Redwood doesn't host your Milvus today; most customers either keep their vector DB and call Redwood for embeddings/rerank (hybrid), or use a managed vector index through partners. For throughput-sensitive flows we recommend colocating the index near the rerank layer (same region / private peering) or using our Dedicated with VPC peering.
02:38 Priya Singh: for dims — if we go from 1536 to 768, how much quality drop should we expect? we ran a few offline tests but unsure about production impact.
02:49 Dana Park: it depends on model and data. Redwood Optimize suggests candidate sizes + quantization profiles; usually 768 can be a good tradeoff for many corpora with minimal impact if you compensate with rerank. quantization (e.g., 8-bit) can reduce storage/cost but sometimes affects nearest-neighbor recall. we can run A/B evals on your dev set.
03:10 Rhett Morales: can you walk through a recommended hybrid architecture? like, embeddings hosted by Redwood but index in Milvus, and rerank in Redwood?
03:21 Dana Park: yeah typical pattern — Redwood hosted API generates embeddings (or you push embeddings from your pipeline via batch), store them in Milvus. For queries, you get ANN candidates from Milvus, call our rerank endpoint with those candidates (we stream tokens and run cross-encoder). If you want lower latency at scale, Dedicated with VPC peering reduces hop latency and gives reserved GPU throughput for rerank.
03:44 Samir Shah: also batching and caching matter — if you have repeated prefixes or similar queries, our prefix/KV cache avoids repeated rerank. But for very spiky traffic Dedicated or private infra is often simpler.
03:56 Jules Carter: about private — what does the VPC deployment look like? data path, control plane — we need to satisfy our security team.
04:04 Samir Shah: for Redwood Private, the control plane can be private and we deploy inference nodes in your VPC or on-prem. you manage KMS and network. we also have audit logs and support SAML SSO, RBAC. I'll share the diagram.
04:18 Rhett Morales: and SOC 2?
04:21 Samir Shah: yes Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. we'll share the security pack.
04:25 Priya Singh: cost — can you ballpark CPU vs GPU cost for rerank? like per-1k queries?
04:31 Dana Park: ballpark is tricky — for hosted, per-token + per-request pricing; for rerank-heavy workloads you often save with Dedicated because GPU amortizes across requests. I'll put together a cost example for 1M queries/month with the candidate sizes and dims you gave.
04:48 [crosstalk] Jules Carter: and the burst handling?
04:50 Dana Park: we have autoscale/burst capacity on Dedicated; plus can configure overflow to hosted or fallback smaller models. so you can have predictable baseline capacity and burst buffer.
05:03 Priya Singh: about model variants — can we pin model versions and have automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model if load spikes?
05:10 Dana Park: yeah that's in the rollout policy — pin primary model and define fallback variants. our runtime does model routing by policy.
05:17 Rhett Morales: how invasive is integrating Redwood API? our stack is python microservices with a Milvus sidecar.
05:23 Samir Shah: integration is straightforward — SDKs in Python. for embed-only you call our embeddings endpoint. for rerank we accept candidates and contexts. we have examples for Milvus + Redwood in our docs.
05:36 Priya Singh: one friction is we currently have on-prem data that can't leave the VPC for compliance. would Private deployment require full air-gap?
05:47 Samir Shah: we have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments — Redwood Private can be deployed fully inside your network; control plane can be customer-managed. it is more of an enterprise engagement.
05:58 Jules Carter: if we go Private, how are updates and maintenance handled?
06:03 Dana Park: updates are either customer-driven (you pull our release) or we coordinate secured upgrade process. support tiers include assistance.
06:10 Rhett Morales: ok can we talk specifics of the perf test? I want to validate p95 tail for rerank with 200 candidates and our dataset.
06:18 Dana Park: plan: Jules provides sample dataset and QPS profile; Dana will create test harness that simulates ANN fanout + rerank; run tests on Dedicated emulator and hosted to compare. target: reproduce your 2k burst and measure p95/p99 latencies.
06:32 Priya Singh: also include eval for dims 1536 vs 768 and quantized 8-bit.
06:37 Dana Park: yes we'll include model variants and rerank batch sizes. we'll also measure cost per query.
06:44 Samir Shah: good. Rhett, what's your timeline for a pilot?
06:48 Rhett Morales: ideally a pilot in the next two weeks, internal stakeholders need to see numbers before Q3.
06:55 Samir Shah: ok we'll aim to start baseline tests next week. I'll get pricing and security docs out today or tomorrow.
07:02 Jules Carter: one more, what's the integration pattern for streaming responses? sometimes our rerank is interactive.
07:08 Dana Park: we support streaming for generation; for rerank we stream scores back as we process candidates if you want incremental results — but for cross-encoder rerank we usually return a batched ranked list.
07:22 Priya Singh: any gotchas on tokenization differences between our local models and Redwood models for rerank?
07:28 Dana Park: yeah small differences can happen. we recommend canonicalizing inputs and we provide consistent tokenizer versions for rerank models. we'll include tokenizer notes in the perf plan.
07:40 [timestamp jump: mid-call deeper technical dive]
20:05 Dana Park: diving into batching — at high QPS you want to balance batch size vs latency. Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching with max latency SLOs; you can set target SLO and runtime will adapt. example: for small cross-encoder BERT-ish reranker, batch of 8–16 gives best throughput with acceptable latency.
20:26 Priya Singh: what about memory pressure with 200 candidates?
20:30 Dana Park: we stream candidates and only materialize top-k for rerank; KV cache helps if many candidates repeat. GPU memory for rerank depends on model size — with quantized 16/8-bit we can reduce memory.
20:45 Jules Carter: network peering — do you support private link or AWS peering?
20:49 Samir Shah: yes VPC peering and private link options exist depending on cloud. for Dedicated we often set up VPC peering for minimal hop.
20:57 Rhett Morales: are there customers with similar scale you can point to?
21:02 Samir Shah: a few analytics customers run dedicated rerank with 1–3k QPS peaks; we'll anonymize case studies.
21:12 Priya Singh: on the vector DB side, are there connectors for Milvus to reduce fetch latency?
21:18 Dana Park: we have example connector patterns and recommended configs — shard placement, replicas, similarity metric tuning. often the wins are in sharding hotspots and colocating rerank.
21:29 [pause — background noise, muffled]
21:45 Rhett Morales: quick question about costs for storage — if we move to 8-bit quantized embeddings in Milvus, how do you recommend indexing?
21:54 Dana Park: use IVFPQ or HNSW depending on recall targets; quantization reduces storage and speeds up ANN, but test for recall hit. Redwood Optimize can run a sim to predict recall loss.
22:10 Priya Singh: ok if we summarize next steps — Jules share dataset, Samir send pricing/security, Dana set up perf plan, pilot next week — correct?
22:20 Samir Shah: yep that's right. I'll also include a recommended architecture diagram for hybrid (Redwood embeds + Milvus index + Redwood rerank).
22:31 Rhett Morales: any blockers from our side — I need exec sign-off for Dedicated spend — will review numbers.
22:37 Samir Shah: understood. we'll make the cost comparison clear.
22:41 [closing minutes — recaps and small clarifications]
45:02 Samir Shah: thanks everyone — expect the pricing and docs by Monday. Dana will reach out to coordinate the perf test. Jules, Priya, thanks for the details.
45:15 Rhett Morales: thanks, this was helpful.
45:18 Priya Singh: thanks all.
45:20 Jules Carter: thanks.
